items.title: "Papa Jack" Laine and Mrs. "Papa Jack" Laine Interview, 1960-05-23
items.q: There was a nigga by the name of Green. He's dead. He used to tell me a whole lot of this stuff, too.

ctx.x: Give you a little breeze. Oh! I have the mic pointed the other way. I don't think it'll pick up the sand. Uh, what other kind of parties did you play? Any other kind of special parties or anything else?

No, nothing but balls. The balls were the balls of course and picnics. Yes. Sure. But parties like that. Weddings and surprise parties and something like that. You know. How many nights a week did you work? Well, I'll tell you. Some weeks I'd be going putting air every night. Putting air every night. I'd be playing. Yeah. Every night. Every night. Even when I'd play at Millenburg. I'd play at Millenburg. I'd play at Millenburg. We'd start at Millenburg playing out there at nine o'clock in the morning. Understand…

I was going to ask about some more of these tunes, like the Dixieland One Step, they call it. La Rocca put his name on all of those. Skeleton, Django, Fidgety Feet, Sensation. He claims he wrote all of those numbers. Do you remember any of those other tunes?
